findings.title: Untrusted search term is concatenated into SQL, enabling injection
findings.evidence: The query now embeds the caller-provided term directly into the SQL text and executes it without parameters, so any single quote or SQL fragment in term changes the statement semantics.
findings.evidence_quote: q = "SELECT * FROM docs WHERE title LIKE '%" + term + "%'"
findings.recommendation: Restore parameterized SQL, e.g. keep the placeholder and pass the pattern as a bound parameter: use 'SELECT * FROM docs WHERE title LIKE ?' with '(f'%{term}%',)'.

findings.title: Searches with apostrophes now fail because quoting is no longer escaped by the driver
findings.evidence: The execution call no longer supplies bound parameters, so a term such as O'Reilly produces invalid SQL like LIKE '%O'Reilly%'. This is a reachable regression for normal user input.
findings.recommendation: Use bound parameters instead of interpolating term into the SQL string so embedded quotes are escaped correctly by the database driver.
